mappings.note: How the chapter bridges Preparatory-Stage curiosity into formal Science. A statement about the discipline and the learner's temper, goal level; no competency covers stage transition.
Questions that cannot be answered in Grade 6, and science as a years-long journey. The 'developmental' clause of CG-SCI1; not CG-SCI2, since no process skill is exercised.

Crushed ice melting faster: parts (i)-(ii) are observation and hypothesis (C-SCI2.1-LO-1), part (iii) demands the cause -- greater exposed surface area (C-SCI2.2-LO-1). Not C-SCI2.2-LO-2, because the item asks WHY rather than merely to describe the melting.

Leaves folding at night: the student poses the question and plans a multi-day observation (C-SCI2.1-LO-1) and supplies a reason tied to water loss and darkness (C-SCI2.2-LO-1), which is the frame's own 'adaptations of plants with their habitats' example.

Sugar dissolving at three temperatures, with part (iv) asking what else must be held identical. A controlled investigation; C-SCI2.1-LO-1 rather than C-SCI2.2-LO-1 because fair testing, not the cause, is what part (iv) marks.

Sonia groups household objects by whether the magnet attracts them. Classifying by an observable property is C-SCI1.2-LO-2; not -LO-1, since she sorts a whole set rather than contrasting two named materials.

Pendulum length versus period: an investigation with one variable changed (C-SCI2.1-LO-1), and part (iii) turns on timing ten swings to reduce error, which is measuring a physical quantity (C-SCI2.3-LO-1). One of the few items in this chapter where the measurement outcome is genuinely earned.
